decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add ... bookmarks.” Client round 1: “I can save links”; client round 2 confirms, “I pasted a link.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented flow permits saving a bookmark from a URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents the initial “Add bookmark” flow. Client round 1 reports that it “asks me to type in the title and the description,” that “the icon seems to just be the first letter,” and requests automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval while retaining editability.
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: automatic metadata collection was absent and bookmark items used a letter rather than the required favicon. The client identified the mismatch and supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 includes “edit ... bookmarks”; maker round 2 says “Fetched text remains fully editable.” Client round 2 verifies, “I could still edit the text before saving.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: together, the presentations establish editing collected title/description before saving and editing saved bookmarks afterward.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 states only “edit ... bookmarks.” Neither client response establishes whether URL, title, description, tags, and markdown note are all editable.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the editable-field scope is unspecified, so conformity or divergence cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 explicitly lists “delete bookmarks”; client round 1 says the other presented management functions “all works for me.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark deletion is presented without evidence of a conflicting behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents tag-related management and filtering. Client round 1 explicitly reports, “I can ... tag them.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: assigning tags to bookmarks is observed as working.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 lists “tag filtering”; client round 1 confirms that tagging and the presented features work.
decisions.note: Implementation review: selecting tags to filter bookmarks conforms to the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 states only “Search with ⌘/Ctrl + K.” The client says “search” works but does not address searched fields, case handling, `#tag`, Boolean/group syntax, or quoted phrases.
decisions.note: Implementation review: generic search is demonstrated, but the record cannot establish whether its required scope and query semantics conform or diverge.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents “Multiple sorting options.” Client rounds 1 and 2 both confirm sorting as part of the working application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the list can be sorted using multiple choices, conforming to the sort-key requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 lists “archive, restore”; client round 1 says archiving keeps unwanted bookmarks from “cluttering the list.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: archive hides bookmarks from the default list and is reversible.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents archive and restore separately from delete: “archive, restore, and delete bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented controls distinguish reversible archiving from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents archive and restore, while the client confirms archived items leave the main list; neither presentation or response identifies a separate archive-only list.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the record does not establish whether archived bookmarks can be viewed in the required separate perspective.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 enumerates automatic retrieval of “page title, description, and favicon” but not the required preview image. Client round 2 repeats those three retrieved fields and says, “That’s exactly what I was after,” without mentioning the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Revised implementation review: the metadata fix remains incomplete because preview-image collection is omitted. The client does not state that expectation or explicitly accept its absence, so the broad approval is not an accepted divergence.
